characterization_methods.purpose: determine tensile properties (YS, UTS, UE, TE, n, r̄)

characterization_methods.key_findings: mean grain size of 6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti is just below 70 µm (between 60 and 80 µm gridlines), coarser than traditional IF steel
characterization_methods.purpose: compare mean grain size of Fe-Al low-density ferritic steels with traditional IF steel

comparative_performance.qualitative_result: higher strength than traditional high-strength IF steel (IF-Rephos) due to strong solid-solution strengthening by Al

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: ductility, strain hardening exponent, normal anisotropy factor
comparative_performance.qualitative_result: similar ductility and n, higher r̄ than DP500 and HSLA350

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot casting is the first step in the typical laboratory thermomechanical route for Fe-Al-(C) ferritic sheet steels (this Fe-6.8Al-0.0035C-0.1Ti alloy belongs to the Fe-Al-(C) ferritic class).
Fairly high coiling temperature used for ultralow C or interstitial-free type Fe-Al-(C) alloys.
t_final = 1 mm; cold rolling (rather than warm rolling) is applicable because the alloy contains <8 wt.% Al.
Final annealing after cold rolling; b0071 notes 800–850 °C has been used in laboratory studies for ferritic alloys because of their limited sensitivity of phase transformation to temperature.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve (Fig. 10, red curve for 6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti) rises to a plateau between the 400 and 600 MPa gridlines extending to ~31-33% strain before a sharp drop.

grain_structure.texture: weakened γ-texture with Al addition (reported for ferritic low-density steels)

structures.overall_structure: fully ferritic microstructure at room temperature

unmapped_findings: Density reduction for ferritic low-density steels is given as 7.5–12.7% in the Fig. 9 legend, and approximately 8 wt.% Al causes ~10% density reduction (b0020); no exact density value is reported specifically for the Fe-6.8Al-0.0035C-0.1Ti sample.

Young's modulus decreases with Al addition (Fig. 12); the Rana et al. [6,20] Fe-Al dataset falls from about 204 GPa at 0 wt.% Al to about 153 GPa near 10 wt.% Al, but no exact Young's modulus value is printed for the 6.8 wt.% Al sample (figure_012, b0061, b0070).
Solid-solution strengthening by Al in ferritic low-density steels is ~40 MPa/wt.% Al (b0053).

It has been suggested that Al content in ferritic low-density steels should be restricted to less than 6.5 wt.% to avoid short-range ordering that increases brittleness and is detrimental to formability; this sample contains 6.8 wt.% Al (b0026).

Stretching and deep drawing behaviors of ferritic low-density steels are reported to be lower than conventional IF steels because of weakening of γ-texture and a decrease of the strain-hardening exponent of the ferrite matrix with Al addition (b0055).
